abstract: How do algorithmic systems regulate worker identities by defining who they are expected to become? Identity regulation research has largely focused on how organizational discourse shapes worker identities. Yet, in platform labour, control is increasingly enacted through algorithmic systems that allocate tasks, monitor performance, and assign reputational scores in real time. Drawing on interviews with delivery partners and platform managers, supplemented by multi-source data, we examine how such systems shape the identities workers are encouraged to adopt or avoid, and how they engage with these processes. We make two key contributions. First, we theorize algorithmic identity regulation as a computational, sociomaterial, and affective form of normative control, whereby digital infrastructures continuously evaluate, rank, and allocate work, recalibrating workers’ identities through ongoing cycles of recognition, visibility, and devaluation. Second, we show how algorithmic identity regulation reshapes dignity at work by rendering recognition continuous, depersonalized, and datafied, making workers’ sense of worth increasingly contingent on algorithmic evaluation. In doing so, we show that algorithmic control not only manages work but shapes how workers define their value, worth, and place in the labour process.

ob.ai_reason: 算法身份规制，算法管理与OB核心议题
ob.tldr: 基于印度外卖配送员与平台管理者的访谈及多源数据，探究平台零工中算法系统如何规训劳动者身份。理论化算法身份规训为计算性、社会物质性与情感性的规范控制，算法通过持续评估、排名和任务分配，在识别、可见性与贬值的循环中重塑劳动者身份。算法控制将工作中的尊严变为持续、去人格化、数据化的认可，劳动者的价值感日益取决于算法评价。

title: Algorithmic identity regulation in the platform-based gig work of Indian food delivery workers
title_zh: 印度外卖配送员平台零工工作中的算法身份规制
